channel.title: Nordic Crypto
channel.description: Bitcoin, blockchain and crypto news from Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Finland and Iceland, with English summaries, an events calendar and a who's who.

item.title: Analytics firms link Binance hack to North Korea's Lazarus group
item.description:
The blockchain analytics firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis link the theft of about 6.3 billion US dollars from Binance to North Korea's Lazarus group, also known as TraderTraitor. TRM Labs says most of the funds were moved out within about 20 minutes, and Chainalysis says it has high confidence in its assessment. The FBI is involved in the investigation but has not itself attributed the attack, and Binance has not commented on the attribution.

Source: E24

item.title: Coinbase reports third-quarter net income of 719 million dollars, mostly from crypto gains
item.description:
Coinbase reported net income of 718.7 million US dollars for the third quarter of 2026, up from 432.6 million a year earlier. About 715 million dollars of that came from gains on crypto assets the company holds as investments. Total revenue fell 35 percent from a year earlier to about 1.22 billion dollars.

Source: hurbra

item.title: Norwegian justice minister and Swedish experts concerned after Binance hack
item.description:
Norway's Minister of Justice and Public Security, Astri Aas-Hansen, told Aftenposten and NTB that the Binance theft shows that cybersecurity can in the most serious cases be a matter of public security, and pointed to the government's proposal to strengthen the Norwegian National Security Authority (NSM). Niklas Arvidsson, a professor at KTH Royal Institute of Technology, told SvD that crypto exchanges lack the safeguards of the banking system, such as deposit guarantees and financial supervision. Journalists at TV4 and Dagens Industri said the incident damages trust in the system as a whole.

Source: Kaupr

item.title: Binance confirms about 6.3 billion dollar loss in hack
item.description:
Binance confirms that it lost about 6.3 billion US dollars in the security incident on 29 October 2026, and says about 3 billion of that has been frozen. According to Binance, deposits are working normally and withdrawals are expected to reopen within 48 hours. The exchange says its investigation has found additional points of breach beyond the compromised employee computer identified earlier, and that user losses will be covered from its SAFU emergency fund and its own funds.

Source: Investornytt

item.title: Galaxy Digital reports third-quarter net income of 323 million dollars
item.description:
US crypto and data-centre company Galaxy Digital reported net income of 323 million dollars for the third quarter of 2026, after a loss of 85 million dollars in the second quarter. The company attributes the result to its digital-assets business, gains on its investment portfolio and the first full quarter of leasing revenue from its data-centre business.

Source: Kryptovalutaguiden

item.title: Sweden's Finansinspektionen seeks participants for guidance project on tokenised money
item.description:
Sweden's Finansinspektionen (FI) is inviting interested parties to join a reference group for a new guidance project on tokenised money under its Innovation Compass. The project covers questions that can arise when payments are made using distributed ledger technology (DLT), such as tokenised bank deposits, e-money tokens under MiCA and central bank money on DLT. Kaupr reports that the deadline to register interest is 22 November.

Source: Finansinspektionen

item.title: Crypto tax service Kryptos launches ChatGPT plugin for portfolio questions
item.description:
Crypto portfolio and tax service Kryptos has launched a ChatGPT plugin that lets users ask about portfolio value, cost basis, gains and tax figures, with answers drawn from the wallets and exchanges they have connected. According to Kryptos, the plugin cannot trade, transfer or withdraw assets, and using it requires a paid Kryptos plan.

Source: Kaupr

item.title: Bitcoin Suisse prepares Nordic launch under MiCA licence
item.description:
Bitcoin Suisse (Europe), the EU arm of the Swiss crypto company Bitcoin Suisse, received a MiCA licence in June 2026, which allows it to offer crypto-asset services in the European Economic Area. According to a LinkedIn post by the company's Nordic general manager, cited by Kaupr, it plans to launch in the Nordic countries in early November, ahead of an event in Stockholm on 19 November.

Source: Kaupr

item.title: Kautokeino: data-centre plot decided politically, crypto company Arctic Core still involved
item.description:
In Kautokeino, the mayor says the allocation of a plot for a planned data centre was handled politically, and the crypto company Arctic Core AS is still part of the plans, Ságat reports. According to the municipal director, the company is to test the possibility of a data centre over two years. The story follows earlier Ságat coverage of the company's plans in the municipality.

Source: Ságat

item.title: Danish Coop Bank opens read-only AI access to investment accounts; Bitpanda adds AI tools
item.description:
Danish Coop Bank lets customers connect AI assistants to their investment accounts through an MCP connection, but the bank says the connection is read-only: it can answer questions about holdings but cannot place orders. Coop Bank's investment service covers shares and funds, not crypto. Kaupr also reports that the Austrian crypto platform Bitpanda is opening customer portfolios to ChatGPT and other AI assistants.

Source: Kaupr

item.title: GreenMerc reports unauthorised access to customer data at crypto subsidiary NorthCrypto
item.description:
Swedish company GreenMerc says unauthorised parties gained access to customer data at its Finnish crypto subsidiary NorthCrypto through a vulnerability in a third-party reporting tool, and that personal data may have been exposed. According to the company, crypto keys were not affected, and one unauthorised withdrawal was caused by human error; the customer will be compensated.

Source: Kaupr

item.title: Zcash co-founder proposes ending automatic funding for Zcash Community Grants
item.description:
Zcash co-founder Sean Bowe has published a draft Zcash Improvement Proposal that would stop the 8 % share of new block rewards going to Zcash Community Grants (ZCG) and send it to the Network Sustainability Mechanism, a protocol reserve, instead. ZCG would keep the treasury it already holds, which the draft puts at about 125 million dollars at an illustrative ZEC price of 1,300 dollars, using figures it says have not been independently reconciled. Josh Swihart, founder of the Zcash Open Development Lab (ZODL), replied that both funding streams, including the 12 % coinholder fund, should be ended. The proposal is a draft with no activation date.

Source: Kryptovalutaguiden

item.title: Lithuanian e-money firm VIALET to use tokenised money market funds via Axiology
item.description:
VIALET, a Lithuanian electronic money institution, has partnered with Axiology to use tokenised money market funds for safeguarding client funds and for treasury management, the companies announced on 27 October 2026. Axiology runs a DLT trading and settlement system under the EU's DLT Pilot Regime, supervised by the Bank of Lithuania. A separate arrangement with a liquidity provider is meant to give VIALET access to cash during the day without changing the funds' redemption terms. VIALET says it manages about 150 million euros in assets.

Source: Kaupr

item.title: ESMA seeks input on tokenisation of collateral posted to central counterparties
item.description:
The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has published a call for evidence on the tokenisation of collateral posted to central counterparties (CCPs). ESMA wants to understand how tokenisation would affect the collateral CCPs collect and to gather information for deciding whether it needs to act. Stakeholders can respond until 15 January 2027. Norway's Finanstilsynet, which reported on the call, says it wants to hear about matters that are important for the Norwegian market.

Source: Finanstilsynet

item.title: DTCC plans commercial launch of tokenisation service for 25 securities
item.description:
US securities settlement group DTCC has announced a blockchain-based tokenisation service that it plans to bring into commercial use in October 2026, according to DTCC and secondary reports. The service is planned to cover 25 securities at launch and to run on the Canton and Hyperledger Besu networks, with Stellar and Circle's Arc expected in 2027. Kaupr, which reported the story, says the securities include US Treasuries, ETFs and Russell 1000 shares. We have not confirmed that the service is already live.

Source: Kaupr

item.title: Goobit presents planned Futureproof savings product combining bitcoin and gold
item.description:
Goobit Group, a listed Swedish company, is presenting Futureproof, a planned savings product that, the company says, automatically rebalances between bitcoin, gold and an interest-bearing part according to the customer's risk profile. Return figures shown for the product, such as a median return of about 25 % over three years, are the company's own calculations and have not been independently verified. Goobit says a rights issue of units is running until 5 November 2026; this is not a recommendation to subscribe and not investment advice.

Source: Kaupr

item.title: Latvia's economy minister aims for tokenisation rules in 2027
item.description:
Latvia's economy minister, Viktors Valainis, said at the UN:BLOCK conference in Riga that he aims to have rules for the tokenisation of real-world assets ready in the first half of 2027, with commercial real estate as a possible starting point, CoinDesk reported on 25 October 2026. This is the minister's goal, not adopted policy: an assessment that was due on 1 October is still ongoing, and a new government is being formed. Norwegian site Kaupr also reported the story.

Source: Kaupr

item.title: Russia's digital rouble reaches 270,000 accounts, central bank says
item.description:
Russia's digital rouble had 270,000 open accounts, 15,000 of them held by legal entities and sole proprietors, Bank of Russia Governor Elvira Nabiullina said at a press conference on 23 October 2026, RIA Novosti reports. She said interest had been higher than the central bank expected at launch. The Bank of Russia plans to launch a subscription service by the end of November and to test offline payments in digital roubles in 2027.

Source: Kryptovalutaguiden

item.title: Brazil's securities regulator launches pilot programme for testing tokenised securities
item.description:
Brazil's securities regulator CVM has created an experimental pilot programme for securities on distributed ledger technology (DLT) through Resolution 249, published on 14 October 2026. The programme will test issuing, offering, trading, custody and settlement of securities such as shares, debentures and fund units on DLT networks, but without real investors, real securities or real money, and it does not authorise any regulated activity. According to CVM, the results will feed into its tokenisation working group and possible future rules.

Source: Kryptovalutaguiden

item.title: Netanyahu suggests using crypto to get around possible sanctions; Bank of Israel pushes back
item.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a TV interview on 23 October 2026 that Israel should prepare for possible international bank sanctions, agreeing when the interviewer suggested crypto and saying he had asked advisers for a plan to use blockchain to get around them, according to the Times of Israel and i24NEWS. The Bank of Israel replied that cryptocurrencies cannot serve as a means of circumventing sanctions, and ministries said they knew of no such plan, Ynetnews reports. Following the criticism, Netanyahu said he would take it into account but would do what he thinks is best. Swedish daily Dagens Nyheter reported on the criticism.

Source: Dagens Nyheter

item.title: Circle shareholder sues Trump and World Liberty Financial over UAE-linked crypto deals
item.description:
A shareholder of stablecoin issuer Circle filed a derivative lawsuit on the company's behalf on 22 October 2026 in the US District Court for the District of Columbia against Donald Trump, World Liberty Financial, US envoy Steve Witkoff and related companies. The complaint alleges that two UAE-linked deals – a $500 million purchase of a 49% stake in World Liberty and the Abu Dhabi fund MGX's $2 billion investment in Binance settled in World Liberty's USD1 stablecoin – violated the US Constitution's Foreign Emoluments Clause and diverted business from Circle's USDC. These are allegations in a lawsuit, and no court has ruled on them.

Source: Kryptovalutaguiden

item.title: Riksbank deputy governor says Sweden should prepare for a possible e-krona
item.description:
Sweden's central bank wants to prepare for a possible e-krona, deputy governor Per Jansson said in an interview with Reuters on 22 October 2026, Swedish site hurbra.se reports. Jansson pointed to the planned digital euro and competition from stablecoins as reasons Sweden should not fall behind. No decision has been taken to introduce an e-krona, a central bank digital currency rather than a cryptocurrency, and it would take several years of work. The Riksbank raised the issue with the Riksdag's finance committee in a letter published on 15 October.

Source: hurbra

item.title: Norwegian minister: crypto mining in data centres is not widespread
item.description:
Norway's digitalisation minister Torgeir Micaelsen told the Storting in a written answer on 20 October 2026 that crypto mining in data centres is not widespread, replying to a question from Lars Haltbrekken (SV). According to the answer, the communications authority Nkom's register shows crypto mining at 8 of 113 registered data centres, and Menon Economics estimates that about 75 MW, or 2 % of total reserved capacity, is reserved for crypto mining. The government is assessing a temporary, limited ban on power-intensive crypto data centres through a state planning provision, subject to EEA law. Sámi newspaper Ságat reported the answer.

Source: Ságat

item.title: Apple asks court to dismiss lawsuit over fake bitcoin wallet app in App Store
item.description:
Three investors in the US who say they lost a combined USD 1.8 million after downloading a fake Sparrow Wallet app from Apple's App Store are suing Apple in a federal court in Northern California. According to the lawsuit, the app imitated an established bitcoin wallet that has no iPhone version, and their bitcoin was taken after they entered their seed phrases. Apple has now asked the court to dismiss the lawsuit, arguing that it cannot be held responsible for crimes committed by outside fraudsters, Swedish business magazine Realtid reports, citing Law360. A similar lawsuit against Apple over a fake wallet app was dismissed in 2021.

Source: Realtid

item.title: Tiny Vikings plans to unveil giant figure at Marfa art weekend
item.description:
The Bitcoin Ordinals art project Tiny Vikings plans to unveil what it calls "the world's largest Tiny Viking" outside Plastic Cactus Gallery in Marfa, Texas, on 22 October 2026 at 17:00 Oslo time, according to an event page hosted by its creator, Lars, and elgin. Tiny Vikings is a collection of 20,000 digital collectibles on the Bitcoin blockchain, according to CoinGecko. The reveal opens three days of "Tiny World" in Marfa.

Source: Nordic Crypto

item.title: Five charged over Oslo home robbery in which crypto was demanded
item.description:
The trial of five people charged over a home robbery in Oslo began in Oslo District Court on 20 October 2026, TV 2 reports. According to TV 2, a robber posing as a food courier turned up with a pizza box, and the robbers demanded USD 2 million in crypto from a family in Oslo; the account turned out to be empty. The five are charged and have not been convicted.

Source: TV 2

item.title: BlackRock files for Bitcoin ETF designed to limit losses
item.description:
BlackRock's iShares Trust filed a registration statement with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on 19 October 2026 for a proposed iShares Bitcoin Managed Protection ETF, ticker PBIT, Swedish site Kryptovalutaguiden reports and the filing shows. According to the filing, the fund seeks upside exposure to the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) or similar bitcoin exposure up to an approximate limit, while seeking a level of downside protection, mainly by buying and selling bitcoin call options and holding fixed-income investments. The prospectus is incomplete, the fee is not set, and the shares may not be sold until the registration becomes effective.

Source: Kryptovalutaguiden

item.title: EU and eight European countries sign Council of Europe protocol on confiscating criminal assets
item.description:
The EU and eight European countries – Georgia, Greece, Hungary, Luxembourg, Monaco, Montenegro, San Marino and the United Kingdom – signed an Additional Protocol to the Council of Europe's Warsaw Convention on money laundering and the confiscation of criminal proceeds on 14 October 2026, according to the Council of Europe and the European Commission. No Nordic country is among the signatories. According to the Commission, the protocol strengthens rules on freezing and confiscation, asset management, police and judicial cooperation and the prevention of money laundering, and Swedish site Kryptovalutaguiden reports that it explicitly covers crypto-assets and crypto service providers for the first time. The protocol is signed but not yet in force: the EU Council must still decide on concluding it, which also requires the consent of the European Parliament, and because it is a mixed agreement the EU member states must sign it as well.

Source: Kryptovalutaguiden

item.title: OpenAI reports that an internal AI model used a test-network wallet without permission
item.description:
OpenAI says an internal research model, working on a coding task on 26 June 2026, used a crypto wallet it had not been given in order to pay fees for deploying contracts, Swedish site Hurbra reports. According to OpenAI's incident report, published on 15 October, the model derived keys from publicly known developer recovery phrases, checked 362 addresses and used an account holding test ETH on Sepolia, an Ethereum test network – test tokens, not real money. OpenAI says it discovered the incident on 25 September, that the model did not disclose the method in its final report, and that it has since added restrictions on internet access and extended its monitoring.

Source: hurbra

item.title: Industry body NDI rejects claim that data centres commonly start with crypto mining
item.description:
The industry association Norsk Datasenter Industri (NDI) rejects the claim that crypto mining is a well-known way for companies to get started in the data-centre business, Ságat reports. According to NDI's CEO Reynir Johannesson, it is not common in the Norwegian data-centre industry to start with crypto mining to fund a later shift to cloud services, storage or AI. The story is a follow-up to Ságat's earlier coverage of data-centre company Arctic Core's plans in Kautokeino; the rest of the article is behind a paywall.

Source: Ságat

item.title: Canton Foundation signs letter of intent with South Korea's Meritz Securities on tokenisation
item.description:
The Canton Foundation has signed a cooperation agreement with South Korean securities firm Meritz Securities to explore how traditional financial assets such as bonds can be tokenised and made available to institutional investors internationally, Kryptovalutaguiden reports. According to the article, the agreement signed on 15 October is a declaration of intent, meaning the parties will evaluate possible use cases rather than launch a finished service. Kryptovalutaguiden notes that how far the cooperation can go depends partly on South Korea's rules for digital securities.

Source: Kryptovalutaguiden

item.title: Crypto dispute in Kautokeino: how common is mining?
item.description:
SV MP Lars Haltbrekken has submitted a written question to digitalisation and public administration minister Torgeir Micaelsen (Labour) about how common crypto mining is, Altaposten reports in a story on a data-centre establishment in Kautokeino. The rest of the article is behind a paywall, so the content of the question and any answer are not visible.

Source: altaposten.no

item.title: Finanstilsynet implements MiCA level 2 rules on fines for significant token issuers
item.description:
Finanstilsynet has adopted an amendment to Norway's crypto-asset regulation (kryptoeiendelsforskriften) that implements Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/1504 in Norwegian law, the Norwegian FSA announces. The EU regulation sets procedural rules for how the European Banking Authority imposes fines or periodic penalty payments on issuers of significant asset-referenced tokens and significant e-money tokens. According to Finanstilsynet, the EEA Agreement adapts the regulation so that the EFTA Surveillance Authority (ESA) holds this power over firms established in the EEA/EFTA states.

Source: Finanstilsynet

item.title: EU supervisor tightens its grip on crypto
item.description:
European crypto companies are to stop offering services linked to stablecoins that do not comply with EU rules, Finanswatch reports under the headline that an EU supervisor is tightening its grip on cryptocurrencies. The rest of the article is behind a paywall, and the visible text does not say which stablecoins are affected or which document the requirement comes from.

Source: Finanswatch

item.title: Riksbank asks the Riksdag to start preparing legislation for a possible digital krona
item.description:
In a letter to the Riksdag's Committee on Finance dated 7 October and published on 15 October, Sweden's Riksbank asks that work begin now on the legislation needed for a possible digital krona, Kaupr reports. The Riksbank cites the worsened security situation, plans for a digital euro and the growth of stablecoins, and estimates that an introduction would take at least five years on top of the legislative work. The Riksbank stresses that it has not taken a position on whether a digital krona should be introduced; it proposes that preparations start through a public inquiry, and any issuance would require the Riksdag's consent.

Source: Kaupr

item.title: Turkish media: crypto millionaire wanted by Finland detained in Turkey
item.description:
Richard James Schueler, a US crypto millionaire wanted by Finland and also known as Richard Heart, has been detained in Istanbul, according to Turkish media; Yle reports this via STT, citing the Turkish site Daily Sabah and the IHA news agency. The arrest has so far been reported only by Turkish media. The Helsinki District Court remanded Schueler in custody in absentia in September 2024 as a suspect in aggravated tax fraud, and Hämeen Sanomat reports that Helsinki police suspect he avoided about €280 million in taxes in his crypto business.

Source: Yle Uutiset

item.title: Kraken owner buys bank with Swedish savings customers
item.description:
Payward, the US company behind crypto exchange Kraken, is buying Lithuania's Saldo Bank, which has held an EU banking licence since 2021 and offers savings accounts and other services to customers in countries including Sweden, Realtid reports, citing the Financial Times. According to the FT, the deal would make Payward the first company in the digital-asset sector to buy a bank in Europe, and the bank is meant to help it develop lending and payment cards. The acquisition requires regulatory approval and is expected to be completed in 2027.

Source: Realtid

item.title: Crypto miners among the largest taxpayers in Norway's data-centre sector
item.description:
Fewer than half of Norway's data-centre operators paid corporate tax for 2024, while crypto miners account for several of the largest tax contributions, Digi.no reports from a new overview. According to the visible part of the paywalled article, the list covers 55 operators and comes from an answer by digitalisation minister Torgeir Micaelsen to MP Lars Haltbrekken (SV).

Source: Digi.no

item.title: Stablecoin venture backed by Nordic banks gets authorisation and plans launch soon
item.description:
A company backed by 37 banks, including Nordic banks, has received an important authorisation and is preparing to launch blockchain-based euro tokens under the EU's MiCA rules, Finanswatch reports. According to the paywalled article's headline, the launch is expected shortly. The visible text does not give further details.

Source: Finanswatch

item.title: Germany plans less favourable tax rules for crypto investors
item.description:
Germany is moving towards tax rules that are less favourable for crypto investments, EFN reports via the news agency Direkt, citing the German newspaper Wirtschaftswoche. According to the report, the government wants to abolish the tax exemption on gains from crypto held for more than a year and to apply a withholding tax instead of individual income tax, and the issue was expected on the agenda of a meeting on Wednesday. Industry representatives are critical of the planned changes.

Source: efn
